Excessive synthesis and secretion of VLDL particles
Deficiency of intrahepatic acetyl- CoA substrate
questions.explanation: Biochemically, Increased intracellular [NADH]/[NAD+] ratio is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: 5. Which amino acid has a lipotropic effect?
questions.explanation: Biochemically, Methionine is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the biochemical basis of non alcoholic fatty liver (NAFLD)?
options: Decrease FFAs uptake by the liver
Decrease lipoprotein production by the liver
Impaired TAG synthesis in the liver
Eating excess unsaturated fatty acids in diet
questions.explanation: Biochemically, Decrease lipoprotein production by the liver is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which cellular elements are characteristically least likely to be found in an amebic liver abscess compared to typical pyogenic abscesses?
options: Extravasated red blood cells Correct Answer: C
questions.explanation: Pathologically, Macrophages and lymphocytes is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A patient with chronic hepatitis B infection undergoes liver biopsy. Some hepatocytes show a characteristic finely granular eosinophilic cytoplasm due to accumulation of HBsAg. What are these cells called?
questions.explanation: Pathologically, Ground-glass hepatocytes is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 55-year-old man with chronic liver disease develops hepatocellular carcinoma. Which of the following exposures is an important risk factor for development of HCC?

questions.text: A patient is diagnosed with hepatitis E virus infection. Which of the following statements regarding hepatocellular carcinoma is correct?
options: HEV is a major cause of HCC
Chronic HEV infection is the most important cause of HCC
HEV is strongly associated with HCC
HEV is not considered a major predisposing factor for HCC
HEV invariably progresses to cirrhosis and HCC
questions.explanation: Pathologically, HEV is not considered a major predisposing factor for HCC is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 48-year-old man presents with hepatomegaly, skin pigmentation and diabetes mellitus. Laboratory investigations show increased iron stores. Genetic testing reveals a defect involving the HFE gene. Which condition is most likely?

questions.text: A 42-year-old man with a chronic, asymptomatic liver condition undergoes an elective liver biopsy during evaluation for elevated serum transaminases. questions.explanation: Pathologically, Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 32-year-old woman presents for a routine physical examination and mild right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort. Which of the following is the most significant predisposing factor for the development of this patient's liver lesion?
questions.explanation: Pathologically, Combined oral contraceptive use is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 52-year-old man presents with chronic fatigue, hyperpigmentation of the skin ("bronze diabetes"), and pain in his second and third metacarpophalangeal joints. A liver biopsy is performed, and Prussian blue staining highlights heavy blue intracellular iron deposits within hepatocytes. Which of the following molecular mechanisms is the primary underlying cause of this patient's condition?
options: Mutation of the HFE gene resulting in decreased hepcidin synthesis
Loss-of-function mutation in the ATP7B gene causing decreased ceruloplasmin binding
Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts led by anti-mitochondrial antibodies
Deficiency of \alpha_1-antitrypsin leading to misfolded protein accumulation in hepatocytes

Binding of ammonia and  washing out colon
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Binding of ammonia and  washing out colon is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the medical management of active bleeding from esophageal varices?
options: Nitrates should be administered alone as first-line emergency monotherapy
Non-selective beta-blockers are the drug of choice to arrest acute ongoing hemorrhage
IV vasopressin is mandatory first, then nitroglycerin is added
Octreotide acts by dilating splanchnic arterioles to increase portal perfusion
Isosorbide mononitrate monotherapy is given as a rapid bolus to stop bleeding
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, IV vasopressin is mandatory first, then nitroglycerin is added is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following mechanisms best describes the therapeutic action of octreotide in treating acute bleeding esophageal varices?
options: Direct V1-receptor activation, causing mesenteric vasoconstriction
Systemic venodilation to counteract peripheral vasoconstriction
Inhibition of the release of peptides contributing to hyperdynamic circulation
Acidification of colonic contents to trap ammonia
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Inhibition of the release of peptides contributing to hyperdynamic circulation is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following drugs decreases portal venous blood flow and is used in the management of variceal bleeding?
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Propranolol is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following adverse effects is particularly associated with aminoglycosides?
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Nephrotoxicity is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following is the regimen of choice in managing ascites in hepatic patient?
options: Using frusemide alone at high dose
Decrease sodium intake while increasing water intake
High protein diet to compensate hypoalbuminemia
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Combination of spironolactone and frusemide is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Following liver transplantation, the complete cessation or avoidance of corticosteroid usage is most closely evaluated or managed in patients undergoing transplantation for which underlying condition?
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Autoimmune disease is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following immunosuppressive agents used in liver transplantation acts by inhibiting calcineurin, thus preventing the expression and synthesis of IL-2?
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Cyclosporine is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A liver transplant patient with pre-existing renal impairment requires maintenance immunosuppressive therapy. Which of the following immunosuppressive agents is contraindicated in this patient?
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Cyclosporine is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A patient with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) undergoes liver transplantation and receives corticosteroids for immunosuppression. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach to corticosteroid use?
options: Long-term high-dose corticosteroids to maintain immunosuppression
Gradual corticosteroid withdrawal to reduce risk of HCC recurrence
Abrupt corticosteroid withdrawal to eliminate tumor recurrence
Progressive corticosteroid escalation to maximize immunosuppression
Complete corticosteroid replacement to enhance antitumor immunity
questions.explanation: Pharmacologically, Gradual corticosteroid withdrawal to reduce risk of HCC recurrence is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: What type of vaccine is commonly used for immunization against Hepatitis A Virus (HAV)?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Inactivated vaccine is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A patient is diagnosed with acute hepatitis B infection. Which of the following hepatitis viruses can occur as a coinfection with HBV?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, HDV is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 35-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection presents for routine follow-up evaluation. Laboratory testing is performed to assess his viral replication status and infectivity level. The presence of which of the following serological markers in his blood best indicates high active viral replication and hyper-infectivity?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, HBeAg is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Control and eradication of Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection represent which level of prevention for Hepatocellular Carcinoma?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Primary prevention is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 25-year-old healthy, unvaccinated man presents 5 days after household exposure to a confirmed Hepatitis A case. He has no underlying medical conditions or vaccine contraindication. What is the most appropriate Post- Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) management?
options: Single dose of hepatitis A vaccine alone
Single dose of hepatitis A immunoglobulin (IG) alone
Combined hepatitis A vaccine and immunoglobulin (IG)
Combined hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) and hepatitis B vaccine
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Single dose of hepatitis A vaccine alone is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following hepatitis viruses is associated with a markedly increased risk of mortality in pregnant women?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is primarily transmitted from person to person through:
options: Ingestion of fecally contaminated water and raw food
Inhalation of infectious respiratory airborne droplets
Exposure to infected blood and body fluids
Direct casual contact and sharing of personal equipment
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Exposure to infected blood and body fluids is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following serological markers is most useful for diagnosing acute hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection during the window period?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, IgM anti-HBc (HBcAb IgM) is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) is a defective virus that strictly depends on the helper function of which of the following viruses for a productive infection?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary mechanism of action of Sofosbuvir (Sovaldi) in the management of Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection?
options: Inhibition of HCV NS5A viral protein
Blockade of viral entry into host hepatocytes
Stimulation of host cell interferon- alpha receptors
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Inhibition of viral RNA polymerase is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 35-year-old sewer worker presents to the emergency clinic with high fever, severe myalgia, jaundice, and renal impairment. A diagnosis of Weil's disease is suspected based on his occupational exposure and multiorgan presentation. Which of the following is the primary laboratory method used to confirm the diagnosis of this infection?
options: Serological testing for antibodies in serum
Stool examination for ova and parasites
Routine blood culture on MacConkey agar
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Serological testing for antibodies in serum is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: How many doses are required for the primary vaccination schedule of hepatitis A vaccine in an immunocompetent individual?
questions.explanation: The primary vaccination schedule for inactivated Hepatitis A vaccine (e.g., Havrix, Vaqta) consists of two doses administered 6 to 12 (or 18) months apart to achieve long-term protective immunity in immunocompetent individuals.

questions.text: Which of the following hepatitis viruses does NOT normally cause chronic hepatitis or cirrhosis?
questions.explanation: HEV (like HAV) is transmitted enterically via the fecal-oral route and causes acute, self-limiting hepatitis without causing chronic hepatitis or cirrhosis in immunocompetent individuals, unlike HBV, HCV, and HDV.

questions.text: The window period of an infectious disease is best defined as the period:
options: Between exposure and development of detectable markers of infection
During which the patient is always symptomatic
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Between exposure and development of detectable markers of infection is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: 1.  liver biopsy from a patient with chronic hepatitis B shows hepatocytes with a finely granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm giving a “ground-glass” appearance. This finding is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Hepatitis B infection is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: A 45-year-old doctor performed laboratory tests for hepatitis C virus and the results were as follows: positive antibody ELISA test, positive RT-PCR for viral RNA. How would you interpret?
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Current infection is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Window period in hepatitis B viral infection is characterized by
questions.explanation: Microbiologically, Presence of anti-HBc IgM is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a risk factor for peptic ulcer disease (PUD)?
questions.explanation: Clinically, Therapeutic use of paracetamol is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Which of the following is the investigation of choice for confirming the diagnosis of peptic ulcer disease (PUD)?
questions.explanation: Clinically, Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.

questions.text: Complications of GERD include all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Clinically, Gastric adenocarcinoma is the correct finding as assessed in GIT past examination guidelines.
